segments.text: Math is the magic that powers AI, but there's a catch.
You ask AI questions in words, and AI operates using numbers.
Look at this chat interface.
You ask, what's the best of Avengers movie?
The AI answers, most people point to Avengers Endgame.
It's the big payoff to a decade of films and it broke box office records.
Infinity War is the other top pick if you like a darker ending.
You put words in and you get words back.
So how do your words become numbers that the AI can actually use?
The most obvious idea is to assign a unique number to every single word in every language.
You type the word, the AI gets the number.
But that system breaks down incredibly fast.
People constantly invent new words, names, and slang.
They make typos. They include things like emojis and write code.
Even if you built a list of a million words, you still couldn't cover everything a human might type.
Instead of giving every word its own number,
AI uses reusable pieces of text called tokens.
This board outlines the building blocks for language.
A token can be a whole word or just part of one.
The collection of all possible tokens is the vocabulary.
Notice how unbelievable goes in, and three separate tokens come out.
Unbelievable.
You can see how the vocabulary saves space by reusing those pieces.
The piece un starts unbelievable, unmatchable, and unusual.
Reuse the pieces, build more words.
Because of this reuse, the vocabulary doesn't need to create a new entry for every newly invented word.
Before you send a message, engineers decide how text will be split.
A program analyzes massive collections of text to build that vocabulary.
Each reusable chunk is assigned a unique number called its token ID.
This ID is just an address in the vocabulary.
The model uses those same tokens and IDs during training and when you chat.
When you hit send, step one is starting with text.
Step two, a tokenizer breaks your text into reusable chunks.
In step three, the tokenizer looks up token IDs in its vocabulary.
Un is 359, Belie is 32898, and Vable is 24694.
Tokenization turns text into token IDs the model can use.
Look at this comparison.
When you see the word cat, you have instant understanding of the animal.
But the AI starts purely with a token ID.
The tokenizer converts cat to ID4719.
A token ID identifies the token, meaning comes later.
This list shows how AI chops up text.
In example two, basket ball becomes two tokens, basket and ball.
Example four covers spacing and symbols.
iHeartAI splits into i, then a space with a heart, then a space with AI.
Notice that SP marks a leading space.
That shows how spaces attached to the chunk that follows them, resulting in three tokens total.
Finally, complex non-standard text.
The web address shown on the board in example five breaks into eight strange chunks.
Once the AI calculates its reply, its answer comes out as a stream of numeric token IDs, not words.
The tokenizer acts as the final translator.
It converts those IDs back into pieces of text and joins them into the readable answer on your screen.
Words become numbers.
That lets AI work with your language using math.
